messages:
IncidentsBot: 🚨 ALERT: high 429 rate observed for tenant Hera Financial (enterprise-vpc, pool: hera-dedicated-3). Origin: realtime-payment + risk-eval endpoints. 429 spike started ~1768007600. Aggregated 5xx/4xx: 429 dominating.

Matt S.: pinging oncall, this looks customer-facing — @Anita R. are you available?

Anita R. (oncall): oncall here. seeing the alert, joining. how many hit requests are we seeing and which backend is the hot path?

Kai L. (devops): metrics snippet: ```
> pool=hera-dedicated-3
requests last 5m: 12.3k
429s last 5m: 3.9k (31%)
avg token rate/user: up 4x vs baseline
cpu/gpu: 85%/92%
connections: hitting concurrency cap -> overflow -> 429
```

Anita R. (oncall): thanks. probable noisy tenant or client-side loop. can we isolate by tenant tag and apply temp per-tenant rate cap?

Kai L. (devops): yep. starting tenant isolation runbook. running: `rictl pool patch hera-dedicated-3 --isolate-tenant tenant-73 --apply-rate 100r/s`

Matt S.: who owns customer comms? Elaine C. from CS? need to tell Hera we're doing an emergency mitigation and might route some traffic.

Elaine C. (CS): I'll DM their technical lead and open a bridge. message: "We're seeing elevated rate limits causing 429s. We're isolating noisy traffic and preparing a temporary capacity bump. ETA 15-30m." Anyone want to add technical details?

Anita R. (oncall): add: "We'll apply a temporary contract-level override (emergency lift) and route traffic to a lower-cost model variant for non-latency-critical requests."

IncidentsBot: ACTION: started runbook #vpc-rate-lift (id: rb-2026-03-15-hera). Paging SRE rotation for escalation.

Kai L. (devops): isolation applied. tenant-73 shows 92% of 429s before isolation, now 429s dropped ~60% for pool but overall traffic still ~1.7x baseline.

Matt S.: looks promising. we still need short-term capacity. @Elaine, can sales/legal ok emergency override for contract HERA-2024-ENT? Need +2x token quota for 2 hours.

Elaine C. (CS): looping SalesOps and Legal. pinging @sales-ops. Also prepping a one-off invoice note.

DevOps - Kai (later): fallback routing in progress: map Hera realtime -> hera-fallback-variant (quantized q4_1, ~30% token cost reduction). Command: ```
rictl route insert --tenant hera --from realtime-payment --to hera-fallback-variant --pct 100 --ttl 2h
```

Anita R. (oncall): while Sales approves, we should also reduce request rate client-side where possible. posting suggested header to customer: ```
X-Redwood-RateLimit-Suggest: 50r/s
X-Redwood-Model-Variant: hera-fallback-variant
```

Matt S.: also enabling short-lived burst capacity: `scale up hera-dedicated-3 --gpus +4 --ttl 2h` — note this will take ~90s to spin up.

IncidentsBot: Deploy job queued: deploy-id d-88231 -> scaling step started. ETA 02:00.

Kai L. (devops): scaling finished. pool GPU utilization back to 60%. 429s dropped to ~5% in last 3m.

Anita R. (oncall): good. initiating post-change checks: run quick evals against realtime-payment and risk-eval to confirm responses still within SLO.```
check script: ```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"prompt":"healthcheck"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/realtime-payment | jq .status
```

Anita R. (oncall): healthchecks green. latency slightly up for fallback variant but within 95th pct SLO.

Elaine C. (CS): SalesOps confirmed emergency lift approved for +2x tokens for 2 hours. Legal acknowledged. I've updated the customer: "We've applied a temporary capacity bump and are continuing to monitor. Expect gradual improvement over next 10m."

Matt S.: summary for incident timeline to include in postmortem: detection -> tenant isolation -> fallback routing -> scale-up -> contract override. Need owner for RCA and telemetry capture.

Anita R. (oncall): I'll take RCA lead. will collect KV cache hit patterns, per-tenant token distributions, kernel selection logs, and autoscale timings. tagging SRE Team to assist.

Matt S.: any lingering action? keep monitoring for 30m then start rollback plan: revert route & remove emergency scale after confirmation.

Kai L. (devops): putting rollback timers: route TTL 2h, scale TTL 2h, contract override expires in 2h. will send reminders 15m before rollback.

IncidentsBot: NOTE: Customer impact window estimated: 1768007600 - 1768009800 (~36m). 429 rate returned to baseline post-mitigation.

Elaine C. (CS): I logged a customer follow-up task and scheduled a call with Hera for 10:00 PT to discuss long-term mitigations (fairshare quotas, burst policies).

Anita R. (oncall): closing bridge soon. final checks continue. thanks everyone. :tada:

Matt S.: great job. will convert runbook notes to postmortem draft and include suggested platform changes: per-tenant auto-throttles, earlier noisy-tenant detection, contract-burst automation.

SRE Team: acknowledged.

IncidentsBot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: Monitoring mode. Remember to file postmortem and tag with `severity:high`, `customer:Hera Financial`, `type:rate-limit`."
